titleEn: Mild Hypothermia - Elderly Woman in an Unheated Home

patient.name: Edith Lawson
patient.affectEn: sitting in a recliner wrapped in a thin blanket over a housecoat; pale and SHIVERING VIGOROUSLY; slow to respond; knows her name and that she is at home but is muddled about the day and date; apologetic, did not want to bother anyone
patient.speechEn: answers slowly in short, hesitant sentences; polite and cooperative; hearing aid not in, so she sometimes asks you to repeat; does not volunteer information that is not asked for (police and the neighbour can fill in details when asked)

scene.settingEn: Detached house in Chilliwack at 0900 hrs. Dim and very cold inside: a thermometer on the wall reads 8 degrees C; outside it is minus 4 degrees C. Police have opened the front door, letting in more cold air. The patient sits in a recliner in the living room wrapped in a thin blanket, wearing a housecoat that is damp at the back from incontinence. Two days of newspapers lie on the mat. A space heater is unplugged. No heating source running and no CO source running. One patient.
hazardsEn: cold environment: 8 degrees C indoors, minus 4 degrees C outside
front door left open by police - cold air coming in and worsening her heat loss until someone closes it
space heater unplugged; no CO source running (none found)

bystanders.knowsEn: They gained entry for the wellness check and found her awake in the recliner, cold to the touch and 'a bit muddled'. They opened the front door when they came in. They know nothing about her medical history. Will close the door, fetch things or hold doors if asked.

Called for the wellness check because she had not seen her for two days and the newspapers were piling up on the mat. Knows the furnace has been broken since the power outage two days ago. Does not know her medications or medical history.

scene.partnerEn: one partner at your licence level; acts only on your delegation
equipmentEn: oxygen kit with nasal cannula and non-rebreather mask
pulse oximeter with finger and ear probes
PCP only: IV start kit with normal saline, D10W

dispatchEn: 0900 hrs. Code 3 to a detached house in Chilliwack. 82-year-old female, wellness check requested by a neighbour who has not seen her for two days. The furnace has been broken since a power outage. Outside temperature is minus 4 degrees C. Hospital is 15 minutes away.
dispatchUpdateEn: Dispatch adds: police attended, gained entry and report the patient is awake, cold to touch and 'a bit muddled'. Fire is not attending.
arrivalEn: A police officer meets you at the open front door: "She's in the living room. She's awake, but she's cold and a bit muddled." Inside, the house is dim and very cold - a thermometer on the wall reads 8 degrees C - and the open front door is letting more cold air in. Two days of newspapers lie on the mat and a space heater sits unplugged. The neighbour who called is waiting in the hallway. One patient. No heating source running, no CO source.
firstLookEn: An 82-year-old woman sitting in a recliner, wrapped in a thin blanket over a housecoat. She is pale and shivering vigorously, and turns her head slowly toward you; she is slow to respond. The back of her housecoat looks damp.

primary.locEn: Awake with her eyes open spontaneously (AVPU = Alert). Answers slowly; knows her name and that she is at home, but is disoriented to the day and the date. Shivering vigorously.
primary.airwayEn: Clear and self-maintained. She is talking; no abnormal sounds, no secretions.
primary.breathingEn: Respirations 16, regular, adequate depth, equal chest rise, not laboured.
primary.circulationEn: Radial pulse 56, regular and weak - in her cold wrist it takes up to 30-45 seconds of careful palpation to be sure of it. No external bleeding.
primary.rbsEn: Modified rapid body survey: no trauma and no sign of injury from a fall (she says she did not fall); mild dependent edema in both ankles; no focal weakness. The housecoat is damp at the back from urinary incontinence. Skin is given automatically during the RBS: pale, COLD to touch centrally including the trunk and abdomen, dry apart from the damp clothing.
primary.skinEn: pale, cold centrally (trunk and abdomen), dry apart from the damp clothing

history.ccEn: I'm just so cold, dear. Cold all the way through. And I feel ever so weak.

opqrst.oEn: It came on gradually, over the two days since the furnace stopped. The power went out and the heat never came back on.
opqrst.pEn: The blankets helped at first. Nothing seems to help now.
opqrst.qEn: Cold all the way through. I can't stop shivering and I'm stiff all over.
opqrst.rEn: It doesn't go anywhere. I just ache all over.
opqrst.sEn: I feel weaker than I did yesterday.
opqrst.tEn: It's been the same the whole time. Two days now.

history.painScoreEn: It's not really a pain, dear. Just a general ache all over from the cold and the stiffness.

sample.sEn: I'm cold, I can't stop shaking, I'm stiff and achy all over and I feel weak. I'm afraid I wet myself - I was too cold and stiff to get up.
sample.aEn: No allergies that I know of.
sample.mEn: My thyroid pill, the levothyroxine, and amlodipine for my blood pressure. And acetaminophen - Tylenol - when my arthritis is bad. (Only if asked whether she has been taking them: "I think I've missed some of my thyroid pills these last few days." Strengths: "I don't remember, dear.")
sample.pEn: An underactive thyroid, arthritis, high blood pressure, and the doctor told me last year that I have a bit of dementia.
sample.lEn: Half a piece of toast and some tea yesterday afternoon. I haven't eaten much at all. I've mostly been drinking tea.
sample.eEn: The furnace stopped working when the power went out, two days ago. I didn't want to bother anyone, so I stayed in my chair under the blanket most of the time. I didn't fall. (If asked: no chest pain, not short of breath, no alcohol - "No, nothing like that.")

fe.generalEn: I feel weak and I haven't had much appetite. I haven't been myself these two days.
fe.cnsEn: I'm a bit mixed up about the date, I suppose. No headache. No weakness on one side. I didn't fall or hit my head.
fe.respiratoryEn: No cough. I'm not short of breath.
fe.cardiovascularEn: No chest pain. No palpitations, no racing heart.
fe.giGuEn: I've wet myself because I couldn't get up - I was too cold and stiff. No diarrhea. I haven't had much to drink except the tea.
fe.integumentaryEn: My skin feels cold and it looks blotchy. My fingers and toes are cold, but they look all right - nothing black or blistered.
fe.musculoskeletalEn: I'm stiff and aching all over. My arthritis is always worse in the cold.
fe.endocrineEn: I have an underactive thyroid. I think I've missed some of my levothyroxine these last few days.
fe.eentEn: No ear pain. My hearing aid isn't in, so you'll have to speak up. Nothing wrong with my eyes or throat.

findings.headNeckEn: No trauma, no signs of a fall. Mucous membranes dry.
findings.chestLungsEn: Clear and equal at all 6 sites, no crackles. Equal chest rise.
findings.backEn: Sacral skin damp and reddened but intact - no pressure ulcer. No injury.
findings.lowerExtremitiesEn: Mild ankle edema bilaterally. Feet cold and mottled; pedal pulses weak but present. NO frostbite - the toes blanch and refill.
findings.upperExtremitiesEn: Cold hands, no frostbite, circulation, sensation and movement intact, no injury.

vitalsSets.spo2: 89% on a cold finger with a poor trace (peripherally shut down, unreliable); 95% on a warmed ear probe

vitalsSets.unlockNoteEn: after active rewarming and glucose, en route (about 15 minutes after baseline); if glucose is never given set 1 stays current

expected.actionEn: Acknowledge; plan thermometer, warm blankets, hot packs, glucometer, and preheat the ambulance to 30 degrees C
triggers: bring the thermometer and the glucometer
bring warm blankets and hot packs
turn the heat up in the ambulance

expected.actionEn: Anticipate that the ambulance interior must be warmed BEFORE the patient is loaded
triggers: get the back of the truck warm before we load
partner, crank the heater in the ambulance
warm the box before she goes in

expected.actionEn: Verbalize hazards (cold environment, open door worsening heat loss, possible CO from heating attempts - none found), environment, nature of illness (environmental exposure), one patient
triggers: nature of illness is environmental exposure

expected.actionEn: ACT on the environmental hazard: close the door and stop ongoing heat loss before beginning the assessment
triggers: can you close that door please
stop the cold air coming in

expected.actionEn: Don gloves and eye protection
First look: elderly female, shivering, pale, slow to respond, damp clothing, cold room
Assess LOC / AVPU: Alert but disoriented - note that confusion is itself a hypothermia sign
triggers: do you know what day it is

expected.actionEn: Verbalize c-spine not indicated after confirming there was no fall
triggers: she denies a fall so no c-spine

expected.actionEn: Assess airway
triggers: she's talking so her airway is open

expected.actionEn: Assess breathing
Assess circulation, taking 30-45 seconds to confirm a pulse in a cold patient before concluding pulselessness
triggers: feel for a pulse for 30 to 45 seconds
take my time with the pulse because she's cold

expected.actionEn: Modified rapid body survey looking for occult injury, especially a fall she may not recall
triggers: check for injuries from a fall

expected.actionEn: Assess skin temperature CENTRALLY (trunk/abdomen), not just at the hands
triggers: feel her skin on the trunk

expected.actionEn: REMOVE the damp clothing and cover with dry blankets - stopping heat loss is the first intervention
Verbalize the oxygen decision and recognize the unreliable peripheral SpO2 reading in a cold patient
triggers: SpO2 on her finger is unreliable

expected.actionEn: Position of comfort, handle gently, and avoid rough handling
triggers: careful with her when we move her

expected.actionEn: Categorize correctly as non-RTC and justify it with the temperature band and her mental status
triggers: she's alert and shivering so stable

expected.actionEn: Ready to load within 30 minutes, with active rewarming started on scene
Verbalize the temperature thresholds and how the plan would change with severe hypothermia
triggers: if she were severe I would not actively rewarm
severe would be insulate only and rapid transport

expected.actionEn: Establish chief complaint: feeling cold, weak and confused after two days without heating
HxC/C with OPQRRRST/LOTARP plus exposure history: duration, ambient temperature, wet clothing, food and fluid intake, alcohol, any fall
triggers: how long have you been cold
have you been eating and drinking
did you have anything to drink, any alcohol

expected.actionEn: PMHx - hypothyroidism is a key predisposing cause of hypothermia
triggers: do you see a doctor for anything

expected.actionEn: Medications
triggers: have you been taking your medications

expected.actionEn: Allergies
LOI - poor intake contributes to hypoglycemia and reduced heat production
GCS with components
BP by auscultation
Pulse - allow 30-45 seconds in a cold patient and report rate, strength and rhythm
triggers: pulse for a full 30 to 45 seconds

expected.actionEn: Respirations rate/depth/character
Skin assessed centrally, hands-on
Pupils
SpO2 - recognize and comment on an unreliable peripheral reading in a cold patient
triggers: reading is unreliable because she's cold

expected.actionEn: BGL - mandatory with decreased LOC; 3.6 mmol/L is below 4.0 and must be corrected
TEMPERATURE - explicitly required in environmental patients and it drives the entire treatment plan
FE - General health
triggers: how have you been feeling lately

expected.actionEn: FE - CNS (confusion, fall screen)
FE - Respiratory
FE - Cardiovascular
FE - GI/GU (intake and incontinence)
FE - Integumentary (frostbite screen)
FE - Musculoskeletal
FE - Endocrine (hypothyroidism is pertinent and may be the underlying cause)
FE - EENT
Head/neck exam with a fall and trauma screen
triggers: any signs of a fall on the head

expected.actionEn: Chest exam with 6-site auscultation
Abdomen exam - a cold abdomen confirms core cooling
Back exam incl skin integrity after two days in a chair
Lower extremities with a frostbite check and distal pulses
Upper extremities with a frostbite check
Remove wet and cold clothing and cover with dry blankets - the single most important intervention
triggers: get her out of the damp housecoat

expected.actionEn: Correctly classify the hypothermia by temperature and choose ACTIVE rewarming for mild hypothermia
triggers: she's mild so we actively rewarm

expected.actionEn: Preheat the ambulance interior to 30 degrees C before loading
triggers: warm up the back of the ambulance
get the box warm before loading

expected.actionEn: Apply hot packs WRAPPED IN TOWELS to the axillae, groin and neck - never directly against the skin
triggers: heat packs in the armpits and groin
wrap the hot packs so they don't burn her
hot packs on the neck over a towel

expected.actionEn: Correct the BGL of 3.6 with oral glucose 15 g since she is alert with an intact swallow, and recheck
triggers: her sugar is 3.6 so I'll give oral glucose

expected.actionEn: Handle gently and avoid rough movement, which can precipitate arrhythmias in a cold heart
triggers: careful, a cold heart is irritable

expected.actionEn: Reassess ABCs and all interventions after each move
triggers: recheck the hot packs and blankets

expected.actionEn: Second full set of vitals within the non-RTC interval, including a repeat temperature and BGL
triggers: another set with a temp and sugar

expected.actionEn: Confirm the temperature is rising and the LOC is improving; document both trends
Recheck the BGL after oral glucose
Notify the receiving facility with the temperature and exposure duration
Complete hand-off with both temperatures, rewarming method, BGL correction and the social situation
Accurate PCR within 5 minutes

specialEvents.descriptionEn: candidate gives glucose to correct the BGL of 3.6 mmol/L: oral glucose gel to the oral mucosa (or, PCP, D10W IV; or glucagon) - record it together with the drug event
candidate applies hot packs (heat packs) to the patient anywhere on the body, wrapped or not
candidate states that the hot packs are placed directly against her bare skin, with no towel or cloth layer between the pack and the skin
candidate moves or handles the patient roughly or abruptly: drags or yanks her out of the recliner, jostles her or drops her onto the cot, or rushes the transfer
PCP gives a fluid bolus (runs normal saline wide open or orders a set volume such as 20 mL/kg or 500 mL); starting an IV with saline at TKVO is NOT this event

drugs.doseEn: 15 g glucose PO (gel to the oral mucosa) for BGL below 4.0 mmol/L in a patient with sufficient mentation to maintain her airway; repeat at 5 minutes as necessary, no limit; only after baseline vitals including the BGL

IM 0.5-1 mg or IN 3 mg - NOT indicated here: she is alert with sufficient mentation and an intact swallow, so oral glucose is the treatment (EMR: glucagon only for insufficient mentation or an unprotected airway; PCP: only when IV access is unsuccessful). Record drug:glucagon only if the candidate actually gives it.
10-25 g (100-250 mL of 10% solution) IV for confirmed hypoglycemia; would replace oral glucose if her mentation fell
vascular access at TKVO only if she deteriorates; NO fluid bolus is indicated (systolic 104, no signs of shock)

notificationFacts.cc: cold, weak and confused after two days in an unheated house - mild hypothermia with hypoglycemia
notificationFacts.hxcc: furnace broken since a power outage two days ago, indoor temperature 8 degrees C; stayed in a recliner, ate very little, incontinent of urine and sitting in damp clothing; denies a fall; found on a neighbour-requested wellness check
notificationFacts.vitals: GCS 14 (disoriented to time), BP 104/62, pulse 56 regular weak, resp 16, tympanic temperature 33.4 C, BGL 3.6 mmol/L, SpO2 95% on a warmed ear probe; latest GCS 15, BP 112/68, pulse 66, temperature 34.6 C, BGL 5.4 mmol/L
notificationFacts.treatments: door closed and heat loss stopped, wet clothing removed, dried and wrapped in warm blankets, ambulance preheated to 30 degrees C, hot packs wrapped in towels to the axillae, groin and neck, oral glucose 15 g with BGL rechecked, gentle handling; non-RTC, ETA 15 minutes
notificationFacts.findings: shivering, cold centrally, no frostbite, no trauma; hypothyroid and thinks she has missed levothyroxine doses

handoffFacts.cc: generalized cold, weakness and confusion after two days in an unheated house
handoffFacts.hxcc: found on a neighbour-requested wellness check after two days in an unheated house (8 degrees C inside, minus 4 outside) after the furnace failed in a power outage; stayed in a recliner, ate little, incontinent of urine and in damp clothing; denies falling, chest pain or shortness of breath
handoffFacts.initialVitals: GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6, disoriented to time), BP 104/62, pulse 56 regular weak, resp 16 regular, skin pale and cold centrally, dry, pupils equal and reactive but sluggish, SpO2 95% on a warmed ear probe (finger reading 89% unreliable), BGL 3.6 mmol/L, tympanic temperature 33.4 C
handoffFacts.finalVitals: GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6, oriented), BP 112/68, pulse 66 regular and stronger, resp 16, skin pink returning and warmer centrally, pupils equal and reactive, less sluggish, SpO2 96%, BGL 5.4 mmol/L, tympanic temperature 34.6 C; shivering decreasing
handoffFacts.pmhx: hypothyroidism (likely contributing), osteoarthritis, hypertension, mild dementia diagnosed last year
handoffFacts.meds: levothyroxine (thinks she has missed some doses), amlodipine, acetaminophen as needed
handoffFacts.treatments: front door closed to stop heat loss; damp clothing removed, dried and wrapped in warm blankets; ambulance preheated to 30 degrees C before loading; hot packs wrapped in towels to the axillae, groin and neck; oral glucose 15 g with the BGL rechecked; gentle handling throughout; non-RTC transport
handoffFacts.findings: mild hypothermia 33.4 rising to 34.6 C; BGL 3.6 corrected to 5.4; no frostbite (toes blanch and refill), no trauma, sacral skin reddened but intact, mild ankle edema; last ate half a piece of toast and tea yesterday afternoon; socially cannot return home until the furnace is repaired

pcrFacts.cc: Cold, weak and confused after two days in an unheated home (mild hypothermia, temp 33.4 C)
pcrFacts.hxcc: Furnace failed two days ago after a power outage; remained in a recliner, minimal food, incontinent of urine, did not call for help; denies fall, chest pain or SOB; found on a neighbour-requested wellness check
pcrFacts.meds: Levothyroxine (doses possibly missed), amlodipine, acetaminophen prn
pcrFacts.vitals: Set 1 (baseline): GCS 14 (E4 V4 M6), BP 104/62, P 56 regular weak, R 16 regular, skin pale cold centrally dry, pupils equal and reactive but sluggish, SpO2 95% on a warmed ear probe (89% on a cold finger, unreliable), BGL 3.6 mmol/L, temp 33.4 C tympanic. Set 2 (en route): GCS 15 (E4 V5 M6), BP 112/68, P 66 regular stronger, R 16 regular, skin pink returning and warmer centrally, PERL less sluggish, SpO2 96%, BGL 5.4 mmol/L, temp 34.6 C tympanic
treatments: Door closed and heat loss stopped before assessment
Wet clothing removed, patient dried and wrapped in warm blankets
Ambulance preheated to 30 C before loading
Towel-wrapped hot packs to axillae, groin and neck
Oral glucose 15 g for BGL 3.6 (alert, intact swallow); BGL rechecked
findings: Tympanic temperature 33.4 rising to 34.6 C - mild hypothermia, actively rewarmed
GCS 14 disoriented to time, improving to 15 and oriented
No frostbite, no trauma, skin intact; peripheral SpO2 unreliable when cold

trackNotes.emrEn: EMR performs the entire hypothermia guideline: removal of wet clothing, blankets, temperature measurement, active rewarming for mild and moderate hypothermia, preheating the ambulance to 30 degrees C, wrapped hot packs and gentle handling. Oral glucose 15 g is within EMR scope for this alert patient with an intact swallow; glucagon would be used only if she could not protect her airway, so it is withheld here. No IV, no D10W. No Functional Enquiry.
trackNotes.pcpEn: PCP adds the 9-system Functional Enquiry and may obtain vascular access if the patient deteriorates; D10W would replace oral glucose if her mentation fell. No fluid bolus is indicated with a systolic of 104 and no signs of shock. Glucagon is not indicated. Hypothyroidism should be flagged to the receiving team as a likely predisposing cause.

sourcePages: Scenario md-07 (data/practical/scenarios.json): dispatch, scene, primary, transport, history, vitals sets 1-2, FE, exam, interventions, ongoing, handoff. BC Provincial Examination Guidelines (current to June 15, 2026): p.7 Findings in Unstable Adult Patients (severe hypothermia is unstable; this patient is mild); p.11 Primary survey interventions (gradual warming for hypothermia; oxygen indications); p.29 Hypothermia (up to 30-45 seconds to determine pulselessness; remove wet and cold clothing and cover; take a temperature; mild >32 and <35 and moderate >28 and <32: actively rewarm - mild activity if appropriate, preheat the ambulance interior to 30 C, hot packs wrapped in towels, warm blankets; severe <28: do not actively rewarm, insulate, heat the ambulance to 30 C, avoid rough handling); p.54 Hypovolemia (fluid bolus only with SBP < 90 and signs of shock); p.57 Diabetic Emergencies (baseline vitals including BGL first; correct BGL < 4.0 with glucose gel when mentation is sufficient; EMR glucagon only for insufficient mentation or an unprotected airway; PCP D10W 10-25 g, glucagon if IV access fails); p.61 D10W; p.67 Glucagon; p.76 Oral Glucose (15 g PO, repeat at 5 minutes as necessary, only with sufficient mentation to maintain an airway).
